purpose: Check the existing RMSNorm implementation against the newly proved adjacent-map scalar identity and derivative; no model or optimizer change.
oracle: Independent Python binary64 evaluation of a/sqrt(a^2+e) and a/sqrt((1+e)*a^2+e^2), with derivatives e/(a^2+e)^(3/2) and e^2/((1+e)*a^2+e^2)^(3/2). Evaluate at the actual represented input amplitude, with the fixed FP32 epsilon also in FP64 runs.
observation: Existing RMSNorm forward and autograd of its mean output along the unit-RMS all-ones direction. Check one map and two adjacent maps at every cell. Exactly zero oracle outputs require exactly zero observed outputs.
limitations: These are local CPU value/directional-gradient checks. They do not certify floating-point arithmetic generally, arbitrary directions, the full model, the unresolved numerical stress failures, or training behavior.
